ntp_monlist_amplification.title: NTP monlist Amplification (CVE-2013-5211)
ntp_monlist_amplification.description: The NTP daemon responds to the deprecated mode 7 `monlist` command, which returns a list of up to 600 recent peers. This is the basis of the well-known NTP amplification DDoS attack (amplification factor 200-500x).
ntp_monlist_amplification.impact: Attackers can use the server as a DDoS reflector. NTP monlist amplification was responsible for multi-hundred-Gbps attacks in 2013-2014 and is still actively exploited.
ntp_monlist_amplification.remediation: Upgrade ntpd to 4.2.7p26 or later (where monlist is disabled by default). Existing deployments: add `disable monitor` to ntp.conf. For ntpsec (the modern fork), monlist is removed entirely.
ntp_monlist_amplification.evidence_template: NTP monlist response from {{host}} returned peer list — amplification possible.

ntp_version_disclosed.title: NTP Version Disclosure
ntp_version_disclosed.description: The NTP daemon responds to version queries with its software version string. Information disclosure only.
ntp_version_disclosed.impact: Reduces attacker's burden of identifying vulnerable versions for targeted exploitation.
ntp_version_disclosed.remediation: Modern ntpd doesn't expose useful version info by default. If running an older daemon, suppress mode 6/7 queries via `restrict default kod nomodify notrap nopeer noquery`.
